newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent rallies late to close at high of $18.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent rallies late to close at high of $18.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures staged a late rally to finish at the day's high on Monday with market-on-close buying encouraged by gains in U.S. markets, brokers said.
Front month August IPE last traded at $18 a barrel, up 33 cents on the day and 29 cents above the low touched only 45 minues from the close.
IPE brokers said the rally to the psychologically important level was triggered by August WTI breaking above resistance at $19.04 a barrel and a late upturn in NYMEX gasoline.
Brokers said an Iranian call on OPEC to act to stop quota violations by members had done the stronger sentiment no harm but did not itself trigger the rush to buy.
The call was made by Iranian Oil Minister Ghomalreza Aghazadeh, in Vienna for this week's OPEC meeting. He added he was not satisifed with oil prices and lamented the large price fall since January.

"It really does look mainly like profit-taking by sellers," a broker said. He said U.S. funds had stayed out of the action, adding that for much of the session spread action had been the dominant play, he said.
August WTI last traded at $19.16 a barrel, up 27 cents.

IPE gas oil futures closed near the low in a lacklustre performance that failed to penetrate any significant resistance despite support from firmer Brent. Front-month July settled at $160.25 a tonne, $1.75 firmer, after touching a high of $161.
Brent's morning strength was on the back of concern over tension between the United Nations and Iraq, traders said.
The U.N. Security Council adopted a resolution over the weekend threatening Iraq with further sanctions if it does not allow U.N. arms inspectors to search sensitive sites.
It also suspended until the end of October regular 60-day reviews of current sanctions.
